newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares still shaky but up from Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares still shaky but up from Tuesday.

text.p: Russian shares crawled back up to Monday's levels, but remained vulnerable as buyers adjusted to near-record levels set in last week's boom, traders said on Wednesday.
The Russian Trading System's (RTS) 24-equity index climbed 3.11 percent to 276.70 from Tuesday's 268.37 on total volumes of $33.9 million, the NAUFOR brokers' association said.
"It has been a speculative day, with some stocks going up and some down," said Nikolai Chikhachyov, a trader at Rossiisky Kredit Bank.
Rostelekom led the market, closing at $3.49, up from Tuesday's close of $3.42. Mosenergo ticked up a penny to $1.49.
UES was also flat for the day at $0.1530 and Megionneftagas slipped to $5.25 from $5.44.
GUM retail outlets released improved profits for nine months in 1996, but the stock was unchanged at $32.00.
"It is stronger than yesterday, but people are still waiting." said Rinaco-Plus trader Alexander Lobanov.
"They're uncertain and no one is expecing big changes tomorrow -- maybe two percent up or down."
Traders said both Russians and Westerners were buying.
They said Russian banks seeking better returns went into equities when yields fell after Wednesday's Treasury Bill auction.
